result.topic_en: The page finishes the discussion of minimal powers leaving remainder 1, with an example modulo 13 and the uniqueness of the inverse c of b mod d. It then opens Chapter VIII on powers that leave remainder 1 when divided by primes: Fermat's theorem, orders dividing p-1, and the reduction of the exponent to gcd(n, 2p).

241. Ita posito $d = 13$, quia $5^4$ est minima potestas unitatem relinquens, si sit $5c = 13k + 1$,
erit quoque $c^4$ minima potestas unitatem relinquens. Verum ut fiat $13k + 1$ per 5 divisibile, sumi
debet $k = 5\lambda - 2$, eritque $c = 13\lambda - 5$, cujus minimus valor est $c = 8$, ita ut etiam $8^4$ sit
minima potestas per 13 divisa unitatem relinquens.

242. Quicunque autem fuerit numerus $b$ minor quam $d$ ad eumque primus, semper quoque
dabitur numerus $c$, etiam minor quam $d$ ad eumque primus, ut sit $bc = kd + 1$, neque plures. Si
enim duo dentur, ut esset tam $bc = kd + 1$, quam $be = ld + 1$, foret $bc - be = b(c - e)$ per $d$
divisibile, unde ob $b$ et $d$ primos, esset $c - e$ per $d$ divisibile, quod cum $c$ et $e$ sint minores quam
$d$, fieri nequit, nisi sit $e = c$. Hoc autem evenire potest, ut fiat $c = b$, quod semper contingit, si
sit vel $b = 1$, vel $b = d - 1$.

Caput VIII.

De potestatibus numerorum, quae per numeros primos divisae, unitatem relinquunt.

243. Quodcunque residuum potestas $a^n$ per numerum $d$ divisa relinquit, idem etiam relinquent
omnes potestates ejusdem exponentis $(a + \lambda d)^n$, atque si $n$ fuerit numerus par, idem residuum
relinquet etiam potestas $(\lambda d - a)^n$, unde judicium residuorum ad numeros $a$ divisore $d$ minores
revocatur.

244. Sit jam divisor $d$ numerus primus quicunque, et quia binarius nullam habet difficultatem,
ponatur $d = 2p + 1$, eritque $2p$ multitudo numerorum ipso $d$ minorum ad eumque primorum. Jam
si $a$ sit numerus quicunque ad $d$ primus, quod fit dummodo $a$ non sit $d$ ejusve multiplum, vidimus
ejus potestatem $a^{2p}$ per $d = 2p + 1$ divisam semper unitatem relinquere.

245. Saepe autem evenire potest, ut etiam potestas inferior $a^n$, existente $n < 2p$, per eundem
numerum $d = 2p + 1$ divisa unitatem relinquat; tum autem exponens $n$ certo est pars aliquota
ipsius $2p$. Quod ergo si evenit, non solum formula $a^{2p} - 1$, sed etiam formula $a^n - 1$ per numerum
primum $2p + 1$ erit divisibilis.

246. Quod si ergo formula $a^n - 1$ fuerit divisibilis per numerum primum $2p + 1$, erit etiam
formula $a^{mn} - 1$ divisibilis, unde cum formula $a^{2p} - 1$ certo sit etiam per $2p + 1$ divisibilis, erit
etiam differentia $a^{mn} - a^{2p}$, seu $a^{2p}(a^{mn - 2p} - 1)$ divisibilis; quare cum factor $a^{2p}$ divisionen non
admittat, alter $a^{mn - 2p} - 1$ divisibilis sit necesse est, quicunque numerus pro $m$ sumatur.

247. Sit $\lambda$ maximus communis divisor numerorum $n$ et $2p$; ac si formula $a^n - 1$ fuerit divi-
sibilis per numerum primum $2p + 1$, etiam haec formula $a^\lambda - 1$ per $2p + 1$ erit divisibilis. Sit
enim $n = \alpha\lambda$ et $2p = \beta\lambda$, ut $\alpha$ et $\beta$ sint numeri primi inter se, et quoniam tam $a^{\alpha\lambda} - 1$ quam
$a^{\beta\lambda} - 1$ sunt multipla ipsius $2p + 1$, etiam hae formulae $a^{\mu\alpha\lambda} - 1$ et $a^{\nu\beta\lambda} - 1$ erunt multipla. At

methods.what: If bc ≡ 1 (mod d) and b^n is the minimal power ≡ 1, then c^n is also the minimal power ≡ 1 (inverses have the same order)
methods.quote:
si $b^n$ fuerit minima potestas
unitatem relinquens, etiam $c^n$ fore minimam potestatem 1 relinquentem

methods.what: Example: the inverse of 5 mod 13 is 8, found by solving 5c = 13k+1; 8 has order 4 mod 13
methods.quote:
sumi
debet $k = 5\lambda - 2$, eritque $c = 13\lambda - 5$, cujus minimus valor est $c = 8$

methods.what: Existence and uniqueness of the modular inverse c of b modulo d; c = b when b = 1 or b = d-1
methods.quote:
semper quoque
dabitur numerus $c$, etiam minor quam $d$ ad eumque primus, ut sit $bc = kd + 1$, neque plures

methods.what: Residues of powers depend only on a mod d; for even n, (λd − a)^n has the same residue as a^n
methods.quote:
idem etiam relinquent
omnes potestates ejusdem exponentis $(a + \lambda d)^n$, atque si $n$ fuerit numerus par, idem residuum
relinquet etiam potestas $(\lambda d - a)^n$

methods.what: Fermat's little theorem: a^{2p} ≡ 1 mod the prime 2p+1
methods.quote: ejus potestatem $a^{2p}$ per $d = 2p + 1$ divisam semper unitatem relinquere

methods.what: If a^n ≡ 1 with n < 2p, then n divides 2p
methods.quote:

ipsius $2p$

methods.what: If a^n ≡ 1 then a^{mn−2p} ≡ 1, obtained by factoring a^{mn} − a^{2p}
methods.quote:

methods.what: If a^n ≡ 1 mod 2p+1, then a^λ ≡ 1 where λ = gcd(n, 2p); the proof uses a Bézout-type relation μα = νβ + 1
methods.quote:

items.quote:
Quicunque autem fuerit numerus $b$ minor quam $d$ ad eumque primus, semper quoque
dabitur numerus $c$, etiam minor quam $d$ ad eumque primus, ut sit $bc = kd + 1$, neque plures.
items.english: Whatever number b less than d and prime to it may be, there will always be a number c, also less than d and prime to it, such that bc = kd + 1, and no more than one.

items.quote:
tum autem exponens $n$ certo est pars aliquota
ipsius $2p$
items.english: but then the exponent n is certainly an aliquot part (divisor) of 2p.

items.quote:
ac si formula $a^n - 1$ fuerit divi-
sibilis per numerum primum $2p + 1$, etiam haec formula $a^\lambda - 1$ per $2p + 1$ erit divisibilis
items.english: and if the formula a^n − 1 is divisible by the prime number 2p+1, this formula a^λ − 1 will also be divisible by 2p+1.
